name: summary
description: Start here. An overview of the person's Apple Health data, as lil health's Summary shows it: for each everyday metric (steps, heart rate, active energy, walking + running distance, resting heart rate, weight), the latest sample and, for types that add up, today's and the last 7 days' totals; plus the workouts of the last 7 days (today and the 6 days before).

timeZone.description: An IANA time zone, e.g. Europe/London, for days and local times. Defaults to UTC on the remote server and to the Mac's time zone locally. Every output says which it used.
The IANA time zone of the output's days and local times.

pinned.description: Deprecated: always false. lil health no longer has pinned metrics, so `metrics` are always the everyday ones.

metrics.description: The metrics, in the order Summary shows them.

workouts.description: Workouts that started today (by now) or in the 6 days before.

type.description: A HealthKit type identifier, e.g. HKQuantityTypeIdentifierStepCount or HKCategoryTypeIdentifierSleepAnalysis. list_types and search return them.

unit.description: The HealthKit unit of the values, e.g. count, kcal or count/min. Null for category types.

start.description: A time in the output's `timeZone`, to the second, with its UTC offset, e.g. 2026-10-20T08:15:00+01:00.

end.description: A time in the output's `timeZone`, to the second, with its UTC offset, e.g. 2026-10-20T08:15:00+01:00.

value.description: A quantity's value, in `unit`. Null for category types.

categoryValue.description: A category sample's HealthKit value (HKCategoryValue…). Null for quantities.

latest.description: The most recent sample that has started, or null if there's none.

today.description: For types that add up (steps, energy, distance): today's total, as Health counts it. Null for other types, or with nothing recorded today.

last7Days.description: For types that add up: the total over today and the 6 days before. Null for other types, or with nothing recorded in those days.

Prefer this to samples.

name: samples

A type can have many thousands of samples a day: use metric for totals and trends, and this only to look at particular readings. Workouts, medications and health details have their own tools.

title: Health Workout Routes

name: workout_route
description: One GPS route in summary: its distance, elevation gain and loss, bounds, where it starts and ends, and its shape as a simplified line of at most 500 points, with the tolerance used. By a workout's ID (from workouts, when hasRoute is true) or a route's (from workout_routes). A workout's route is the one HealthKit linked to it or, failing that, one linked to no workout that was recorded during it. Its every point, with speed, course and accuracy, comes from workout_route_points, a page at a time: ask for them only when the shape isn't enough. Routes are precise locations.

id.description: A workout's ID, from workouts, or a route's, from workout_routes.

timeZone.description: An IANA time zone, e.g. Europe/London, for days and local times. Defaults to UTC on the remote server and to the Mac's time zone locally. Every output says which it used.
The IANA time zone of the output's days and local times.

time.description: A time in the output's `timeZone`, to the second, with its UTC offset, e.g. 2026-10-20T08:15:00+01:00.

altitude.description: Meters above sea level. Stored as a 32-bit float, so rounded to 2 decimal places, or null if the device didn't know.

tolerance.description: Meters: no point of the route is further than this from the line through points. 5 m, doubled until it keeps at most 500 points.

points.description: The points it kept, in order, the first and last included.

HealthRouteShape.description: Its shape, simplified (Ramer-Douglas-Peucker): enough to draw it, or to tell where it went and when.

workout.description: The ID of the workout HealthKit linked it to, or null if it links none: then workout_route still finds it by the ID of a workout it was recorded during.

start.description: A time in the output's `timeZone`, to the second, with its UTC offset, e.g. 2026-10-20T08:15:00+01:00.

end.description: A time in the output's `timeZone`, to the second, with its UTC offset, e.g. 2026-10-20T08:15:00+01:00.

pointCount.description: How many GPS points it has.

source.description: The app or device that recorded it.

distance.description: Meters along its points, from each to the next on the Earth's surface. The workout's own distance, which the Watch also measures by motion, may differ a little.

elevationGain.description: Meters climbed: every rise from one point to the next, among the points with a known altitude, to 2 decimal places. From GPS, so noisier, and usually higher, than the workout's elevationAscended, which the barometer measures. Null without two such points.

elevationLoss.description: Meters descended, as elevationGain counts climbs.

bounds.description: The box its points fit in, to 5 decimal places (about a meter).

startArea.description: About where it starts: its first point, to 3 decimal places (about 100 m).

endArea.description: About where it ends: its last point, to 3 decimal places (about 100 m).

title: Health Workout Route

name: workout_route_points
description: A GPS route's points, in order, a page at a time: each one's time, latitude, longitude and altitude, speed, course and accuracy. By a workout's ID (from workouts, when hasRoute is true) or a route's (from workout_routes). A workout's route is the one HealthKit linked to it or, failing that, one linked to no workout that was recorded during it. A route has about a point a second, thousands an hour: call workout_route first, whose simplified shape is usually enough, and this only to look at particular stretches. Routes are precise locations.
